title: Why Microsoft Is the ‘Best-Positioned Firm in Tech’ - Barron's | Coolest Cloud Solutions
text:
Why Microsoft Is the ‘Best-Positioned Firm in Tech’ By Jan. 25, 2019 11:03 a.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by Drew Angerer/Getty Images Text size
Microsoft (MSFT) looks like the “best-positioned firm in tech,” argues Morgan Stanley ’s Keith Weiss . He reiterated an Outperform rating and $140 price target on the stock Friday, arguing that investors should buy the stock ahead of its second-quarter report, as Microsoft looks to have more than 30% upside from current levels.
Microsoft shares were up 1.3% to $107.61 in Friday morning trading.
The Back Story: Microsoft was the best-performing tech stock in the Dow Jones Industrial Average in 2018, and in the past 12 months it’s outperformed three-fifths of the FAANG stocks, coming in ahead of Facebook (FB), Apple (AAPL), and Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL). The company has benefited from a shift toward subscription-based services, which produce strong, recurring revenues, and the growth of its Azure cloud-computing division, among other strengths . It’s also a favorite among well-known fund managers .
The Plot Twist : Weiss argues that as IT focus shifts from the public cloud (where hardware, software, and management are controlled by the provider) to a hybrid cloud (a mix of public and private solutions), Microsoft has been gaining market share, amid a backdrop of software growth that’s more stable than some believe. This leads him to believe that the strong secular catalysts driving Microsoft sales should be more than enough to offset any cyclical headwinds in the industry. Thus he’s confident that Microsoft will turn in a strong fiscal second quarter when it reports results on Jan. 30, with commercial cloud gross margins remaining above 60%.
Moving Forward: It’s not just the second quarter that looks robust, Weiss argues. His survey of chief information officers supports his thesis that Microsoft will continue to take share over the next three years. Growth of its on-premise server products and tools keeps him upbeat about the company’s ability to keep up its recent momentum, and he argues the shares still look attractive, despite their recent performance.
